note: Track legato (guitar-techniques), step 1: the trill with fingers 1 and 2 (legato-trill at level new) on three strings, the last one faster in stages.

exercise.title: Hammer-ons and pull-offs, fingers 1 and 2
exercise.why: A hammered note is only as loud as the finger lands, so a trill with no picking lets you hear at once when a finger lands too softly.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome and follow the tab. Pick the first note once, then hammer finger 2 on and pull it off again, one note per beat, with no more picking.
Keep going until the hammered note is as loud as the picked one.
_Rest your hand as soon as it gets tired._

Press Play below to start the metronome. The same trill is now on the A string, which is thicker, so finger 2 has to land harder.
If the pulled-off note is quiet, flick finger 2 a little sideways as it leaves the string.

Press Play below to start the metronome and play the trill on the high E string.
When both notes are equally loud, try a faster stage. Use the Stage selector below to change the tempo, then press Play to start the metronome again.
If a note goes missing at a new stage, go back one stage.
